summary: The statement and proof are correct. The halfspace-mass continuity argument, compact convex-hull attainment, and positive-depth argument establish 0 < Delta <= 1/2 without assuming log-concavity of P. The finite cutting construction preserves convexity, log-concavity of each conditional reference density, its finite first moment, and positive conditioning mass. I checked the cited [Lovasz and Vempala manuscript](https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~vempala/papers/logcon.pdf): Lemma 5.12 on printed page 24 is exactly the centroid halfspace inequality used here and requires no isotropic normalization, continuity, or compact support. Each cut removes at most Delta of the original P mass and at least a 1/e fraction of the remaining Q mass. The floor bounds give P(A_r) >= 1/2 and Q(A_r) <= exp(-ell*r), with 0 < Q(A_r) < 1. Conditional Jensen, including the case P(A_r)=1, yields D + log(2) >= ell/(8*Delta); all rearrangements use positive quantities. The cases d=1, Delta=1/2 with r=1, D=0, and null cutting boundaries introduce no exceptions. Containment in every compact convex supporting set follows from containment in the convex hull of the support. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
